run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: Checked the approved runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook: Step 1 (signup pods, status, logs) done via Kubernetes; Step 2 (payments pods and logs) done; Step 3 (service-to-service connectivity) could not be executed because no exec/port-forward tool exists in this Run, so I inspected the Services and Endpoints instead; Step 4 (Stripe/api-key log patterns) done on the payments pod logs; Step 5 (environment variables) could only be done at the spec level, because secret values cannot be read here. Findings: in namespace app-162 both Deployments were created at 2026-11-25T07:16:32Z by kubectl-client-side-apply at revision 1 / generation 1 (environment provisioning, not a mid-incident restart). The payments-service pod runs, has restartCount 0 and no previous container, but its log states 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' and 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', its /ready and /health return 503, and the payments-service Endpoints object contains only notReadyAddresses and no ready addresses. The two signup-service pods also run with restartCount 0 but log 'ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' every readiness cycle and answer /ready with 503; the Deployment reports unavailableReplicas 2 with Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable) and the signup-service Endpoints object also has only notReadyAddresses. The payments-service Deployment wires STRIPE_API_KEY from Secret app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key; that Secret's value could not be read, so the invalid credential is named by the payments-service runtime log and by the env wiring rather than by a direct secret read. Ruled out by direct observation: no NetworkPolicy, no ResourceQuota and no Ingress in/for app-162, no pod crash/restart/OOM evidence (all containers 'running', lastState empty, no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff events for these pods), Service selectors/ports matching the configured PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL. Prometheus and Jaeger were both SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE during this Run, so no error-rate, latency baseline or trace evidence exists; end-user registration attempts were not observed in the sampled logs. Conclusion is partial: the failing dependency and the object holding the bad credential are identified, but the secret value, the change time and the metrics/trace view are unverified.

claims.text: In namespace app-162 the Deployments signup-service (spec.replicas 2) and payments-service (spec.replicas 1) both report Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable; signup-service has unavailableReplicas 2 and payments-service unavailableReplicas 1, and both Deployments were created at 2026-11-25T07:16:32Z with kubectl-client-side-apply as manager, deployment revision 1 and metadata.generation 1.

Pods signup-service-7c89545dc9-7fd8v, signup-service-7c89545dc9-w89wv and payments-service-6d94c44fdc-4c9s8 are phase Running with container ready=false, restartCount 0, empty lastState and started containers; the Ready and ContainersReady conditions are False with reason ContainersNotReady.

payments-service container log (pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-4c9s8) contains: '2026-11-25 07:16:34,653 - ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' and '2026-11-25 07:16:43,253 - ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', together with 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503' at 07:16:39, 07:16:44 and 07:16:49 and 'GET /health HTTP/1.1" 503' at 07:16:43.

The payments-service Deployment spec maps env STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef name payments-secrets key stripe-api-key (and DATABASE_URL from payments-secrets key database-url, PORT=8080); the content of Secret app-162/payments-secrets could not be read in this Run, so the key value is known only from the payments-service runtime log line.

Both signup-service replicas log a repeating dependency error and readiness failure: '2026-11-25 07:16:39,101 - ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503', repeating at 07:16:44 and 07:16:49 on pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-7fd8v and identically at 07:16:39, 07:16:44 and 07:16:49 on pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-w89wv.

The Endpoints object payments-service in app-162 contains only notReadyAddresses (pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-4c9s8, ip 10.244.0.31, port 8080) and no ready addresses; the signup-service Endpoints object likewise lists only notReadyAddresses for both signup pods (10.244.0.29, 10.244.0.30) and no ready addresses.

Service payments-service (clusterIP 10.96.1.79, port 8080, targetPort 8080, selector app=payments-service) and Service signup-service (clusterIP 10.96.246.241, port 8080, selector app=signup-service) match the pod labels, and the signup-service container env sets PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080, so the configured target name/port resolves to these Services and not to a wrong host.

app-162 has no NetworkPolicy objects, the cluster has no ResourceQuota objects, and there are no Ingress objects matching app-162 or referencing signup-service/payments-service, so those configuration layers hold no object that would explain the refused connection.

No event in the authorized window marks these pods as crashed or evicted: the app-162 event set consists of Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started plus ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate and Deployment ScalingReplicaSet between 07:16:32Z and 07:16:33Z, and no Evicted, OOMKilled or BackOff reason appears for signup-service or payments-service (the cluster-wide Unhealthy/BackOff events belong to kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo pods such as coredns, metrics-server, kube-state-metrics and otel-collector).

The only ConfigMap in app-162 is kube-root-ca.crt; no application ConfigMap exists for signup-service or payments-service, so the fault-injection-style setting candidate set here is limited to the Deployment env wiring and the referenced Secret payments-secrets.

Causal chain supported by the observations: Secret app-162/payments-secrets holds an invalid Stripe key in key stripe-api-key, so payments-service fails its own /ready and /health checks and never becomes ready, so the payments-service Endpoints object has no ready address, so signup-service's readiness check to http://payments-service:8080 is refused (Errno 111), so both signup replicas stay unready and the signup-service Service has no ready endpoints for registration traffic.

Remaining unverified candidate: signup-service's own DATABASE_URL comes from Secret app-162/signup-secrets key database-url, which could not be read; if that value is also wrong or its database unreachable, signup would still fail after payments recovers. No database error line appears in the signup logs sampled in the window, but signup never passed its payments readiness gate, so its database path was not exercised in observable traffic.

Rejected: a NetworkPolicy or resource quota blocking signup-service to payments-service. app-162 holds zero NetworkPolicy objects and the cluster holds zero ResourceQuota objects, and the connection refusal coincides with a payments-service Endpoints object that has only notReadyAddresses.

Rejected: payments-service crashlooping, OOMKilled or evicted as the cause. Its pod is Running, restartCount is 0, lastState is empty, no previous container instance exists, and no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff event names payments-service or signup-service pods.

Rejected: a missing or unresolvable Secret reference preventing payments-service from starting. The payments-service container is in state running with a containerID and the pod reached the Started event, so the secretKeyRef references (payments-secrets stripe-api-key and database-url) resolved and the container's application code is executing; the problem is the value in use, not an unresolved reference.

The signup-side connection refusal is not a wrong-address configuration error: the Service payments-service listens on port 8080 with targetPort 8080 and selector app=payments-service, which matches the payments pod, and PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL is http://payments-service:8080; the refusal is consistent with the Service having no ready endpoint rather than with a host/port mismatch.

Practical next steps: replace the invalid Stripe key in Secret app-162/payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key) through the normal credential-rotation path, then confirm payments-service /ready returns 200 and that the payments-service Endpoints object gains a ready address before expecting signup-service to become ready; per the target's standing instructions, a Stripe/Stripe-API related issue should be routed to the interlock team (that routing instruction is guidance, not evidence).

Advisory checks still worth doing outside this Run: read the actual values of payments-secrets and signup-secrets (not readable here) to confirm stripe-api-key and both database-url entries, capture a real /register request end-to-end after payments-service is ready, and compare signup error rate and latency against a baseline once Prometheus and Jaeger are reachable.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable in this Run (every metrics tool returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query), so there is no ERROR/error-rate series, no request count and no latency baseline for signup-service or payments-service; their health is therefore not assessable from metrics.

Jaeger was unavailable in this Run (traces_list_services and traces_search both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there are no spans showing the signup-service to payments-service call edge, no trace error status and no trace-derived failure rate; note also that the tool's configured trace service list contains 'payment' (the otel-demo service) and no 'signup-service' or 'payments-service' entry, so any trace evidence would come from a differently named entity and this could not be checked.

Secret values cannot be read: the content of app-162/payments-secrets (stripe-api-key, database-url) and app-162/signup-secrets (database-url) is unverified; the invalid Stripe key is known only from the payments-service runtime log line, not from reading the Secret.

No pod exec or port-forward tool exists in this Run, so runbook Step 3 (curl http://payments-service:8080/health from a signup pod) and Step 5 (reading STRIPE/DATABASE env values inside the payments container) could not be carried out; only the Deployment env references and the Services/Endpoints were inspected.

The change_history integration is not configured for this target, so when and by whom the Stripe key (or any payments-secrets value) was changed is unknown, and no object was observed applying the change.

End-user registration impact is unverified: no /register request lines appear in the sampled signup logs (only /ready probes reached the pod), and there is no Ingress for signup-service, so the client path that reported 'users can't register' was not observed.

8 events fell outside the authorized window end and were dropped before the event queries ran, so probe-failure Unhealthy events for the signup-service and payments-service pods, if any, are unknown; the pods were only ~20 s old at query time, so the observed readiness 503s are also within their startup window.

Whether the payments-service database (payments-secrets database-url) is reachable is unknown: payments logs sampled in the window contain only the Stripe error and no database error line, which is not proof of a working database.
next_steps: Correct/rotate the STRIPE_API_KEY value in Secret app-162/payments-secrets and restart payments-service through the normal procedure, then verify its /ready and /health return 200 and that its Service gains a ready endpoint.
Per the target's standing instructions, engage the interlock team for the Stripe/Stripe-API related part of this issue and the capricorn team for any non-Stripe part.
Restore or point the investigation at Prometheus and Jaeger so signup-service and payments-service error rates, request counts and the signup-to-payments span can be checked against a baseline.
After payments-service is ready, drive one real /register request to signup-service and confirm the response, and separately validate the signup-secrets and payments-secrets database-url values.
Add an alert on payments-service readiness/available replicas so a dependency failure surfaces before signup-service becomes entirely unready.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
